# Contract field reference, schema 0.7.7 preview

Status: **preview**. A contract opts in with `fluidVersion: "0.7.7"`; a contract that declares 0.7.6 is unaffected. This page lists the difference between the 0.7.6 schema and the 0.7.7 schema as bundled with the CLI: added fields, fields whose definition changed, and fields removed. A field not listed here has the same type, required flag, allowed values, default and description in both; for those, use the [0.7.6 reference](./contract-0.7.6.md). A definition used at several paths is listed once, at its first path.

Generated from `fluid_build/schemas/fluid-schema-0.7.7.json` in the `data-product-forge` 0.42.0 package (sha256 `649b9bc59bb509b5`). It is the schema `fluid validate` checks a contract against, rendered without edits. To regenerate: `python scripts/gen_contract_reference.py`.

Each table row is one field, addressed by its path from the contract root: `.` descends into an object, `[]` marks the items of a list, and `<key>` stands for any key of a map. **Required** means required inside its parent object; the parent can itself be optional. **Allowed values** lists the enum, pattern and range the schema enforces. An object typed plainly `object` rejects keys the schema does not list; `object (open)` accepts extra keys and `object (free-form)` has no listed keys. A row that begins "Only when ..." exists only under that condition. See [how to read this reference](./README.md#how-to-read-a-row).

- Added: 371 rows
- Changed: 18 rows
- Removed: 0 rows

Consumers match one anchored regex compiled from it; uniqueness comes from the column's key, not from the format. |

| `exposes[].contract.schema[].identifierFormat[].mask` | string | yes | min length 1<br>max length 64 |  | COBOL PICTURE style: 9 is a digit, A an upper-case ASCII letter, X an upper-case ASCII letter or a digit; a backslash makes the next character literal (\\A), and every other printable ASCII character stands for itself. At least one symbol; no repeat counts (write 99999, not 9(5)). |
| `exposes[].contract.schema[].placeholders` | object | no |  |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Placeholder values of this string column: stand-ins for a real value that is not known yet, such as TBD_0042 (RFC-data-rules.md section 4). A value is a placeholder when it equals one of values or starts with one of prefixes, case-sensitively; NULL never is. A placeholder is exempt from the column's own value checks (identifierFormat, validationRules, its enum) and an ordinary value everywhere else. One mustBe\* operator with unit bounds the placeholder rows; without one they are declared and reported, never failed. A sentinel that stands for no value (UNKNOWN for NULL) is a quality\[\] missingValues rule instead. |

Unique within its message (the top level, or the struct it sits in); 1 to 536870911 except 19000 to 19999, which Protobuf reserves. A field number names the field on the wire, so it never changes once data is written. |

| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].expr` | string | no | min length 1 |  | With derive: the column's value, a FLUID SQL/1 expression of the column's type whose static scale fits the column's (wrap a product or a quotient in ROUND(x, s)). |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate` | object | no |  |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): A summary over child rows (RFC-data-rules.md section 1.2): SQL's aggregate, with SQL's null rules and its FILTER clause, declared on the parent expose. count has scale 0, sum its column's scale, min and max their column's type. |

| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate.column` | string | no | min length 1 |  | The child column summarized: none for count, a number of bounded scale for sum, any orderable type for min and max. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate.from` | string | yes | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_]$\|^[A-Za-z0-9_]$` |  | The child expose, an exposeId of this contract. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate.via` | string | yes | min length 1 |  | A relationship the child declares (its semantics.relationships\[\].name) whose to is this expose. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate.filter` | string | no | min length 1 |  | A FLUID SQL/1 predicate over the child row: only children for which it is TRUE count, as in SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE ...). |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].aggregate.ifNone` | string or number | no |  |  | A literal of the summary's type that replaces a NULL summary, as COALESCE would: when no child counts, or every counted child's column is NULL. A date is written 'YYYY-MM-DD', quoted. Without it, sum, min and max of nothing are NULL and count is 0. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].dependency` | object | no |  |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): A functional dependency (RFC-data-rules.md section 1.2): equal values in from mean equal values in to. A row with a NULL from column is not covered; a NULL to value is a value. A key's violating rows are its covered rows minus those that carry its most common to values (the g3 measure). bothWays adds the reverse dependency, counted on its own, and takes one column a side. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].dependency.from` | array of string | yes | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: min length 1 |  |  |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].dependency.to` | array of string | yes | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: min length 1 |  |  |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].dependency.bothWays` | boolean | no |  | `false` |  |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].when` | string | no | min length 1 |  | A FLUID SQL/1 predicate: the rows the invariant covers (every row without it). A row on which a compared value is NULL is covered and usually violates the invariant; write when to leave such rows out. Not on a dependency in v1. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].severity` | string | no | one of `error`, `warning`, `info` | `"error"` | How a consumer reports a violation, in contract.quality\[\]'s words. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBe` | number | no | min 0 |  | Exactly this many violating rows. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBeLessThan` | number | no | min 0 |  | Fewer violating rows than this. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBeLessOrEqualTo` | number | no | min 0 |  | At most this many violating rows. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBeGreaterThan` | number | no | min 0 |  | More violating rows than this. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo` | number | no | min 0 |  | At least this many violating rows. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].mustBeBetween` | array of number | no | min items 2<br>max items 2<br>each item: min 0 |  | From lo to hi violating rows, both included, with lo below hi. |
| `exposes[].contract.invariants[].unit` | string | no | one of `rows`, `percent` | `"rows"` | rows counts violating rows; percent is violating rows times 100 divided by covered rows, and 0 when no row is covered. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry` | object | no | When `kind` is `confluent`: requires `url` |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The registry a produced topic's subject is registered in, on a Kafka binding (platform: kafka, or platform: confluent with format: kafka_topic). The topic is this product's, so forge registers its value schema, derived from contract.schema, through OpenTofu with this compatibility: aws_glue_schema for kind glue, confluent_schema and confluent_subject_config for kind confluent. On any other platform nothing is registered and fluid validate warns; the value is still checked against this definition. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.kind` | string | yes | one of `glue`, `confluent` |  | glue: AWS Glue Schema Registry. confluent: Confluent Schema Registry REST API. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.url` | string | no | matches `^https?://[^/?#@\s]+(?:/[^?#\s]*)?(?![\s\S])`<br>format `uri` |  | kind confluent only, and required there: the registry's REST endpoint, http or https, with no credentials, query or fragment in it (credentials go in auth). Sending anything to the host is subject to the operator's egress policy. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.registryName` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_$#.-]{1,255}(?![\s\S])` |  | kind glue only: the Glue registry's name. Absent: default-registry, the registry Glue uses when none is named. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.subject` | string | no | matches `^[^\u0000-\u001f\u007f]{1,255}(?![\s\S])` |  | The subject (confluent) or schema name (glue) that holds the record value's schema. Absent: &lt;topic&gt;-value, the Confluent TopicNameStrategy name, on both kinds. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.version` | string or integer | no | must be `latest`<br>or min 1 | `"latest"` | The schema version to verify against or read with: latest, or a version number from 1. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.compatibility` | string | no | <details><summary>one of 11 values</summary><code>NONE</code> <code>DISABLED</code> <code>BACKWARD</code> <code>BACKWARD&#95;ALL</code> <code>FORWARD</code> <code>FORWARD&#95;ALL</code> <code>FULL</code> <code>FULL&#95;ALL</code> <code>BACKWARD&#95;TRANSITIVE</code> <code>FORWARD&#95;TRANSITIVE</code> <code>FULL&#95;TRANSITIVE</code></details> |  | The compatibility mode a produced subject is registered with. Glue accepts NONE, DISABLED, BACKWARD, BACKWARD_ALL, FORWARD, FORWARD_ALL, FULL and FULL_ALL; Confluent accepts NONE, BACKWARD, BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE, FORWARD, FORWARD_TRANSITIVE, FULL and FULL_TRANSITIVE. Absent: backward and transitive, BACKWARD_ALL on Glue and BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE on Confluent. A consumed subject's mode is the producer's, so this is not applied to it. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.auth` | object | no |  |  | kind confluent only: the registry credential, as a secret reference, the same shape as kafka-connect schema_registry.auth. Glue authenticates with the job's IAM role. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.auth.secretRef` | string | no | matches `^env://[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`<br>or matches <code>^file:<wbr>//(/(?!&#92;.&#123;1,2&#125;(/&#124;$))&#91;^/&#92;s#?&#92;x00-&#92;x1f&#92;x7f-&#92;x9f&#93;+)+$</code><br>or matches `^(vault\|openbao)://[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_@=+-][A-Za-z0-9_.@=+-]*)+#[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+(\?version=[1-9][0-9]*)?$`<br>or matches <details><summary>a 174-character pattern</summary><code>^(aws-sm&#124;aws):<wbr>//(arn:aws&#91;a-z-&#93;&#42;:secretsmanager:&#91;a-z0-9-&#93;+:&#91;0-9&#93;&#123;12&#125;:secret:&#91;A-Za-z0-9/&#95;+=.@-&#93;+&#124;&#91;A-Za-z0-9/&#95;+=.@-&#93;&#123;1,512&#125;)(#&#91;A-Za-z0-9&#95;.@-&#93;+)?(&#92;?version=&#91;A-Za-z0-9-&#93;&#123;32,64&#125;)?$</code></details><br>or matches `^(gcp-sm\|gcp)://projects/[a-z0-9-]+/secrets/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,255}(/versions/([1-9][0-9]*\|latest))?$`<br>or matches `^(azure-kv\|azure)://[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,24}/[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,127}(\?version=[0-9a-f]{32})?$`<br>or matches <details><summary>a 184-character pattern</summary><code>^(?!(env&#124;file&#124;vault&#124;openbao&#124;aws-sm&#124;aws&#124;gcp-sm&#124;gcp&#124;azure-kv&#124;azure):<wbr>//)&#91;a-z&#93;&#91;a-z0-9+.-&#93;&#42;:<wbr>//(?!&#91;^/#?&#93;&#42;:&#91;^/#?&#93;&#42;@)&#91;^&#92;s#?&#92;x00-&#92;x1f&#92;x7f-&#92;x9f&#93;+(#&#91;A-Za-z0-9&#95;.@-&#93;+)?(&#92;?version=&#91;A-Za-z0-9.&#95;-&#93;+)?$</code></details> |  | NEW in v0.7.7: A reference to a secret held in a store, never the secret itself: a contract names a secret and never carries one. Grammar: &lt;scheme&gt;://&lt;locator&gt;\[#field\]\[?version=n\]. Schemes: env, file, vault, aws-sm, gcp-sm, azure-kv; aliases openbao (vault), aws (aws-sm), gcp (gcp-sm) and azure (azure-kv) are accepted; any other lower-case scheme (such as op://) is passed to the pack that resolves it. #field picks one key of a secret that holds several; ?version= pins a version where the store keeps them. |
| `exposes[].binding.properties.registry.rules` | boolean | no |  | `false` | kind confluent only, on a subject an expose produces, and Avro only: true registers the expose's error-severity row checks (contract.invariants\[\] with a check and no mustBe\* bound) as Confluent data-contract rules (CEL CONDITION rules in mode WRITE, onFailure ERROR) that Confluent's serializers enforce on every record. Other invariants (derive, aggregate, dependency, a check with a bound, a warning or info check) are reported as not enforced by the registry; a check with no exact CEL form is refused. Needs Confluent Platform Enterprise 7.4+ with the rule set extension, or Confluent Cloud's Stream Governance Advanced package. |

| `exposes[].binding.packaging.containers.athenaWorkgroup` | string | no | one of `isolated`, `shared` |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Ownership of the Athena workgroup (aws_athena_workgroup) the product's queries and dbt builds run in. |

The location must be the table's alone: fluid validate refuses a bucket root, a location that holds, or sits inside, another expose's, and a '.' or '..' path segment, and it must not hold the files of a table outside the contract either. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.removeOrphanFiles.enabled` | boolean | no |  | `true` | false declares the block and runs nothing. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.removeOrphanFiles.olderThan` | string | no | matches `^P(?=\d\|T\d)(\d{1,7}W)?(\d{1,7}D)?(T(?=\d)(\d{1,7}H)?(\d{1,7}M)?(\d{1,7}S)?)?$` |  | An ISO-8601 duration of at least P1D (whole days on backend glue), default P3D: a file younger than the longest write is not an orphan yet. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.actions` | array of object | no | max items 20 |  | backend spark: a package's maintenance actions (the fluid_build.maintenance_actions entry points), run first. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.actions[].name` | string | yes | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` |  | The action's name, unique on the table; its commits are stamped with it. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.actions[].kind` | string | yes | matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` |  | The kind's name under the fluid_build.maintenance_actions entry points. |
| `exposes[].iceberg.maintenance.actions[].options` | object (free-form) | no |  |  | JSON values the kind reads. No secret: a kind reads its own. |

### builds

| Path | Type | Required | Allowed values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `builds[].execution.orchestration.airflow.poolPerOutputTable` | boolean | no |  | `false` | NEW in v0.7.7: When true, the generated DAG puts each task that writes an output table in a one-slot Airflow pool named after the table (pool_slots 1), so two DAGs that write the same table do not run together. The locking is Airflow's own pool. A build that writes more than one table (a build with no outputs writes every expose) is refused by validate and by the DAG renderer: declare one output per build or split it. `fluid schedule-sync --airflow-url` creates the pools Airflow lacks (and never changes one that exists); without it the generate and sync reports print the `airflow pools set` lines. Off by default: nothing changes in a DAG unless it is set. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark` | object | no | When `runtime` is `emr-eks`: requires `virtualClusterId`<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-serverless`, `local`): must not set `applicationId`<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-serverless`, `local`): applicationId is only valid with runtime: emr-serverless<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-ec2`, `local`): must not set `clusterId`<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-ec2`, `local`): clusterId is only valid with runtime: emr-ec2<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-eks`, `local`): must not set `virtualClusterId`<br>When not (`runtime` is one of `emr-eks`, `local`): virtualClusterId is only valid with runtime: emr-eks<br>When `runtime` is `glue`: must not set `releaseLabel`<br>When `runtime` is `glue`: releaseLabel is an EMR release; a glue runtime takes glueVersion<br>When `runtime` is one of `emr-serverless`, `emr-ec2`, `emr-eks`: must not set `glueVersion`<br>When `runtime` is one of `emr-serverless`, `emr-ec2`, `emr-eks`: glueVersion is only valid with runtime: glue; EMR runtimes take releaseLabel |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Where and how a Spark build runs. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.runtime` | string | yes | one of `emr-serverless`, `emr-ec2`, `emr-eks`, `glue`, `local` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Where the job runs: EMR Serverless, EMR on EC2, EMR on EKS, an AWS Glue Spark job, or local, a spark-submit on the machine fluid apply runs on (a laptop, or a lab with an EMR 7.x image). One runner and one job config serve all five. A local run writes a table in an Iceberg REST catalog (location.catalog lakekeeper, rest or polaris) on platform local, which the operator's Spark configuration declares. local ignores the AWS runtimes' keys (applicationId, clusterId, virtualClusterId, releaseLabel, glueVersion, executionRoleArn), so a contract written for AWS switches to local with one overlay line. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.mode` | string | no | one of `streaming`, `batch` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. streaming: a long-running Structured Streaming job. batch: a job that runs to completion. Absent: streaming when properties.stream is set, else batch. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.applicationId` | string | no | matches `^[0-9a-z]{1,64}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. emr-serverless only (runtime local ignores it): an existing EMR Serverless application. Absent: the forge-managed application shared by the product's domain. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.clusterId` | string | no | matches `^j-[0-9A-Za-z]{1,254}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. emr-ec2 only (runtime local ignores it): a running EMR cluster (j-...). Absent: a transient cluster that ends with the job. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.virtualClusterId` | string | no | matches `^[0-9a-z]{1,64}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. emr-eks only, and required there (runtime local ignores it): the EMR on EKS virtual cluster. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.glueVersion` | string | no | matches `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?![\s\S])` | `"5.0"` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. glue only (runtime local ignores it): the AWS Glue version of the job. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.releaseLabel` | string | no | matches `^emr-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+((-[a-z0-9]+)*-(latest\|[0-9]{8}))?(?![\s\S])`<br>When `runtime` is `emr-eks`: matches `^emr-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-(latest\|[0-9]{8})(?![\s\S])`<br>When `runtime` is one of `emr-serverless`, `emr-ec2`: matches `^emr-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?![\s\S])` | `"emr-7.12.0"` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. EMR runtimes only (emr-serverless, emr-ec2, emr-eks; runtime local ignores it): the EMR release, in the form the runtime takes. emr-serverless and emr-ec2 name the release (emr-7.12.0, the default); emr-eks names an image of it, emr-X.Y.Z-latest or emr-X.Y.Z-YYYYMMDD (default emr-7.12.0-latest). 7.12 or later writes Iceberg with Lake Formation credentials. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.executionRoleArn` | string | no | matches `^arn:aws[a-zA-Z0-9-]*:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/[A-Za-z0-9_+=,.@/-]{1,512}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The IAM role the job runs as (runtime local ignores it: a local job runs with the credentials of the machine it runs on). Absent: a least-privilege role forge creates for the build. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.maskKeySecretArn` | string | no | matches `^arn:aws[a-z-]*:secretsmanager:[a-z0-9-]+:[0-9]{12}:secret:.+(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The AWS Secrets Manager secret holding the HMAC key for maskAtIngest: hash. Required when any mapping column sets maskAtIngest (the cross-field check lives in the Spark compiler). |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.sparkConf` | object (map) | no | keys: matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,256}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Spark configuration properties for the job, name to string value (spark.sql.shuffle.partitions: "64"). |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.sparkConf.<key>` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. |
| `builds[].properties.parameters.spark.source` | object | no | at least one of `bootstrapServers` or `mskClusterArn` is required<br>set bootstrapServers (a host:port list) or mskClusterArn (an Amazon MSK cluster)<br>When `bootstrapServers` is set: must not set `mskClusterArn`<br>When `bootstrapServers` is set: set one of bootstrapServers or mskClusterArn, not both<br>When `runtime` is `local`: must not set `mskClusterArn`<br>When `runtime` is `local`: a local run reads source.bootstrapServers: nothing resolves an MSK cluster's brokers for it |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Elsewhere the stream describes what the build's own sql reads. |

| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality` | array of object | no | each item: min properties 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.6: Column-level data quality rules, in ODCS's own shape — the array that is written straight into `schema[].properties[].quality[]` of the exported ODCS v3.1.0 contract, and the array an imported ODCS column's rules are read back into, inline on the column rather than in the importer's pass-through bucket: the ODPS importer merges a resolved port's `contract` block into its output-port stub and discards the sub-import's root `extensions`, so rules left in that bucket were dropped outright by a FLUID → ODPS → FLUID cycle. The ODCS exporter has always replayed this key verbatim and always read it back on import, but `$defs.column` is `additionalProperties: false` and did not define it, so a column written the way the exporter supports was REFUSED by `fluid validate`: the only way to get a hand-written quality rule into a published contract was to write an invalid contract. Optional and additive — a column without it exports exactly as it does today, with the rules forge derives from `required`, the primary-key tag and `validationRules`. Setting it REPLACES those derived rules for that column rather than adding to them, which is what makes an imported ODCS column round-trip byte-for-byte. The authority for an item's contents is ODCS v3.1.0 `$defs.DataQuality`, deliberately not re-declared here (a copy would drift from the vendored schema, and `fluid odcs validate` already checks an emitted document against it); the keys below are the common ones. Every rule should carry an `id`: it is optional in ODCS, but a DQ engine that labels its results by rule id rejects a contract whose rules have none. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].id` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Stable rule identifier, unique within this column's rules. The pattern is ODCS `$defs.StableId`. Rules forge derives itself are named `<column>-<metric>`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].type` | string | no | one of `text`, `library`, `sql`, `custom` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. ODCS quality check type. text = prose; library = one of ODCS's predefined metrics; sql = a query whose result is compared; custom = a named engine's own check. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].metric` | string | no | one of `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues`, `duplicateValues`, `rowCount` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. The five predefined metrics ODCS v3.1.0 defines; a name outside this list is not a library rule. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].arguments` | object (free-form) | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. Extra arguments for the metric — `pattern` (a regex) or `validValues` (a list) for invalidValues, as DataHub's ODCS ingestion source reads them. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].query` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: sql only. The query whose result the comparison operator is applied to. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].engine` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: custom only. The engine that runs the check, e.g. soda, great-expectations, dbt. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].implementation` | any | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: custom only. The check as that engine expresses it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].dimension` | string | no | one of `accuracy`, `completeness`, `conformity`, `consistency`, `coverage`, `timeliness`, `uniqueness` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The data quality dimension the rule measures. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].description` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].severity` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Severity of a failure. ODCS types this as a free string and documents info / warning / error by example. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].unit` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Unit the comparison is in, usually rows (the default) or percent. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].identifierFormat` | array of object | no | min items 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The identifier formats of this string column (RFC-data-rules.md section 3), a list of alternatives. A value has the format when it is one of an alternative's prefixes followed by a string its mask matches. Alternatives must not overlap, a foreign-key column repeats its target column's format or declares none, and placeholders are exempt. Consumers match one anchored regex compiled from it; uniqueness comes from the column's key, not from the format. |

| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].identifierFormat[].mask` | string | yes | min length 1<br>max length 64 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. COBOL PICTURE style: 9 is a digit, A an upper-case ASCII letter, X an upper-case ASCII letter or a digit; a backslash makes the next character literal (\\A), and every other printable ASCII character stands for itself. At least one symbol; no repeat counts (write 99999, not 9(5)). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].placeholders` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Placeholder values of this string column: stand-ins for a real value that is not known yet, such as TBD_0042 (RFC-data-rules.md section 4). A value is a placeholder when it equals one of values or starts with one of prefixes, case-sensitively; NULL never is. A placeholder is exempt from the column's own value checks (identifierFormat, validationRules, its enum) and an ordinary value everywhere else. One mustBe\* operator with unit bounds the placeholder rows; without one they are declared and reported, never failed. A sentinel that stands for no value (UNKNOWN for NULL) is a quality\[\] missingValues rule instead. |

| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality` | array of object | no | each item: min properties 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.6: Column-level data quality rules, in ODCS's own shape — the array that is written straight into `schema[].properties[].quality[]` of the exported ODCS v3.1.0 contract, and the array an imported ODCS column's rules are read back into, inline on the column rather than in the importer's pass-through bucket: the ODPS importer merges a resolved port's `contract` block into its output-port stub and discards the sub-import's root `extensions`, so rules left in that bucket were dropped outright by a FLUID → ODPS → FLUID cycle. The ODCS exporter has always replayed this key verbatim and always read it back on import, but `$defs.column` is `additionalProperties: false` and did not define it, so a column written the way the exporter supports was REFUSED by `fluid validate`: the only way to get a hand-written quality rule into a published contract was to write an invalid contract. Optional and additive — a column without it exports exactly as it does today, with the rules forge derives from `required`, the primary-key tag and `validationRules`. Setting it REPLACES those derived rules for that column rather than adding to them, which is what makes an imported ODCS column round-trip byte-for-byte. The authority for an item's contents is ODCS v3.1.0 `$defs.DataQuality`, deliberately not re-declared here (a copy would drift from the vendored schema, and `fluid odcs validate` already checks an emitted document against it); the keys below are the common ones. Every rule should carry an `id`: it is optional in ODCS, but a DQ engine that labels its results by rule id rejects a contract whose rules have none. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].id` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Stable rule identifier, unique within this column's rules. The pattern is ODCS `$defs.StableId`. Rules forge derives itself are named `<column>-<metric>`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].type` | string | no | one of `text`, `library`, `sql`, `custom` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. ODCS quality check type. text = prose; library = one of ODCS's predefined metrics; sql = a query whose result is compared; custom = a named engine's own check. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].metric` | string | no | one of `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues`, `duplicateValues`, `rowCount` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. The five predefined metrics ODCS v3.1.0 defines; a name outside this list is not a library rule. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].arguments` | object (free-form) | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. Extra arguments for the metric — `pattern` (a regex) or `validValues` (a list) for invalidValues, as DataHub's ODCS ingestion source reads them. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].query` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: sql only. The query whose result the comparison operator is applied to. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].engine` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: custom only. The engine that runs the check, e.g. soda, great-expectations, dbt. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].implementation` | any | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: custom only. The check as that engine expresses it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].dimension` | string | no | one of `accuracy`, `completeness`, `conformity`, `consistency`, `coverage`, `timeliness`, `uniqueness` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The data quality dimension the rule measures. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].description` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].severity` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Severity of a failure. ODCS types this as a free string and documents info / warning / error by example. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].unit` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Unit the comparison is in, usually rows (the default) or percent. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].identifierFormat` | array of object | no | min items 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The identifier formats of this string column (RFC-data-rules.md section 3), a list of alternatives. A value has the format when it is one of an alternative's prefixes followed by a string its mask matches. Alternatives must not overlap, a foreign-key column repeats its target column's format or declares none, and placeholders are exempt. Consumers match one anchored regex compiled from it; uniqueness comes from the column's key, not from the format. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].identifierFormat[].prefixes` | array of string | no | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: matches `^[ -~]*$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Literal prefixes, printable ASCII. One empty prefix when left out. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].identifierFormat[].mask` | string | yes | min length 1<br>max length 64 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. COBOL PICTURE style: 9 is a digit, A an upper-case ASCII letter, X an upper-case ASCII letter or a digit; a backslash makes the next character literal (\\A), and every other printable ASCII character stands for itself. At least one symbol; no repeat counts (write 99999, not 9(5)). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Placeholder values of this string column: stand-ins for a real value that is not known yet, such as TBD_0042 (RFC-data-rules.md section 4). A value is a placeholder when it equals one of values or starts with one of prefixes, case-sensitively; NULL never is. A placeholder is exempt from the column's own value checks (identifierFormat, validationRules, its enum) and an ordinary value everywhere else. One mustBe\* operator with unit bounds the placeholder rows; without one they are declared and reported, never failed. A sentinel that stands for no value (UNKNOWN for NULL) is a quality\[\] missingValues rule instead. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.values` | array of string | no | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: min length 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Whole values that are placeholders. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.prefixes` | array of string | no | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: min length 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. A value that starts with one of these is a placeholder. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBe` | number | no | min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Exactly this many placeholder rows. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBeLessThan` | number | no | min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Fewer placeholder rows than this. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBeLessOrEqualTo` | number | no | min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. At most this many placeholder rows. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBeGreaterThan` | number | no | min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. More placeholder rows than this. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo` | number | no | min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. At least this many placeholder rows. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.mustBeBetween` | array of number | no | min items 2<br>max items 2<br>each item: min 0 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. From lo to hi placeholder rows, both included, with lo below hi. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].placeholders.unit` | string | no | one of `rows`, `percent` | `"rows"` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. rows counts placeholder rows; percent counts them per 100 rows of the expose. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].sharedAttribute` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The attribute this column carries with every other column of the contract that names the same one (RFC-data-rules.md section 5). The owner is the member that every other member reaches through relationships, following to, on exactly one path; on every row whose path reaches an owner row, a member IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the owner. Never inferred from column names, and not semanticType, which stays a kind of value such as email. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].protobuf` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): How this column is written when the topic's value is Protobuf (binding.serialization.value: protobuf). Every column of such an expose, nested struct fields included, needs one. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].protobuf.field` | integer | yes | min 1<br>max 536870911<br>must not be 19000 to 19999 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The column's field number in the .proto forge generates when the topic's value is Protobuf (binding.serialization.value: protobuf). Unique within its message (the top level, or the struct it sits in); 1 to 536870911 except 19000 to 19999, which Protobuf reserves. A field number names the field on the wire, so it never changes once data is written. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].tags` | array of string | no | unique items<br>each item: matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$\|^[a-z0-9]$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Field-level tags for categorization and data governance. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].labels` | object (map) | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Field-level labels for metadata and automation. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].labels.<key>` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Label values are always strings for consistency and tooling compatibility. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.prefix` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Put in front of every key column's name, so a key field can share its name with a value field (a Debezium key repeats the value's id). A mapping names the prefixed column. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.metadata` | array of object | no | min items 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Kafka record metadata, each read as a column. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.metadata[].name` | string | yes | min length 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The column's name, unique among the stream's value, key and metadata columns. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.metadata[].from` | string | yes | one of `topic`, `partition`, `offset`, `timestamp`, `timestamp-type`, `headers`, `leader-epoch` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The metadata the column reads. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.metadata[].description` | string | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry` | object | no | When `kind` is `confluent`: requires `url` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The registry that holds this topic's value schema. The topic belongs to its producer, so forge verifies the subject against schema and never registers it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.kind` | string | yes | one of `glue`, `confluent` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. glue: AWS Glue Schema Registry. confluent: Confluent Schema Registry REST API. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.url` | string | no | matches `^https?://[^/?#@\s]+(?:/[^?#\s]*)?(?![\s\S])`<br>format `uri` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. kind confluent only, and required there: the registry's REST endpoint, http or https, with no credentials, query or fragment in it (credentials go in auth). Sending anything to the host is subject to the operator's egress policy. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.registryName` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_$#.-]{1,255}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. kind glue only: the Glue registry's name. Absent: default-registry, the registry Glue uses when none is named. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.subject` | string | no | matches `^[^\u0000-\u001f\u007f]{1,255}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The subject (confluent) or schema name (glue) that holds the record value's schema. Absent: &lt;topic&gt;-value, the Confluent TopicNameStrategy name, on both kinds. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.version` | string or integer | no | must be `latest`<br>or min 1 | `"latest"` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The schema version to verify against or read with: latest, or a version number from 1. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.compatibility` | string | no | <details><summary>one of 11 values</summary><code>NONE</code> <code>DISABLED</code> <code>BACKWARD</code> <code>BACKWARD&#95;ALL</code> <code>FORWARD</code> <code>FORWARD&#95;ALL</code> <code>FULL</code> <code>FULL&#95;ALL</code> <code>BACKWARD&#95;TRANSITIVE</code> <code>FORWARD&#95;TRANSITIVE</code> <code>FULL&#95;TRANSITIVE</code></details> |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The compatibility mode a produced subject is registered with. Glue accepts NONE, DISABLED, BACKWARD, BACKWARD_ALL, FORWARD, FORWARD_ALL, FULL and FULL_ALL; Confluent accepts NONE, BACKWARD, BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE, FORWARD, FORWARD_TRANSITIVE, FULL and FULL_TRANSITIVE. Absent: backward and transitive, BACKWARD_ALL on Glue and BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE on Confluent. A consumed subject's mode is the producer's, so this is not applied to it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.auth` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. kind confluent only: the registry credential, as a secret reference, the same shape as kafka-connect schema_registry.auth. Glue authenticates with the job's IAM role. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.auth.secretRef` | string | no | matches `^env://[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`<br>or matches <code>^file:<wbr>//(/(?!&#92;.&#123;1,2&#125;(/&#124;$))&#91;^/&#92;s#?&#92;x00-&#92;x1f&#92;x7f-&#92;x9f&#93;+)+$</code><br>or matches `^(vault\|openbao)://[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_@=+-][A-Za-z0-9_.@=+-]*)+#[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+(\?version=[1-9][0-9]*)?$`<br>or matches <details><summary>a 174-character pattern</summary><code>^(aws-sm&#124;aws):<wbr>//(arn:aws&#91;a-z-&#93;&#42;:secretsmanager:&#91;a-z0-9-&#93;+:&#91;0-9&#93;&#123;12&#125;:secret:&#91;A-Za-z0-9/&#95;+=.@-&#93;+&#124;&#91;A-Za-z0-9/&#95;+=.@-&#93;&#123;1,512&#125;)(#&#91;A-Za-z0-9&#95;.@-&#93;+)?(&#92;?version=&#91;A-Za-z0-9-&#93;&#123;32,64&#125;)?$</code></details><br>or matches `^(gcp-sm\|gcp)://projects/[a-z0-9-]+/secrets/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,255}(/versions/([1-9][0-9]*\|latest))?$`<br>or matches `^(azure-kv\|azure)://[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,24}/[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,127}(\?version=[0-9a-f]{32})?$`<br>or matches <details><summary>a 184-character pattern</summary><code>^(?!(env&#124;file&#124;vault&#124;openbao&#124;aws-sm&#124;aws&#124;gcp-sm&#124;gcp&#124;azure-kv&#124;azure):<wbr>//)&#91;a-z&#93;&#91;a-z0-9+.-&#93;&#42;:<wbr>//(?!&#91;^/#?&#93;&#42;:&#91;^/#?&#93;&#42;@)&#91;^&#92;s#?&#92;x00-&#92;x1f&#92;x7f-&#92;x9f&#93;+(#&#91;A-Za-z0-9&#95;.@-&#93;+)?(&#92;?version=&#91;A-Za-z0-9.&#95;-&#93;+)?$</code></details> |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7: A reference to a secret held in a store, never the secret itself: a contract names a secret and never carries one. Grammar: &lt;scheme&gt;://&lt;locator&gt;\[#field\]\[?version=n\]. Schemes: env, file, vault, aws-sm, gcp-sm, azure-kv; aliases openbao (vault), aws (aws-sm), gcp (gcp-sm) and azure (azure-kv) are accepted; any other lower-case scheme (such as op://) is passed to the pack that resolves it. #field picks one key of a secret that holds several; ?version= pins a version where the store keeps them. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.registry.rules` | boolean | no |  | `false` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. kind confluent only, on a subject an expose produces, and Avro only: true registers the expose's error-severity row checks (contract.invariants\[\] with a check and no mustBe\* bound) as Confluent data-contract rules (CEL CONDITION rules in mode WRITE, onFailure ERROR) that Confluent's serializers enforce on every record. Other invariants (derive, aggregate, dependency, a check with a bound, a warning or info check) are reported as not enforced by the registry; a check with no exact CEL form is refused. Needs Confluent Platform Enterprise 7.4+ with the rule set extension, or Confluent Cloud's Stream Governance Advanced package. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.trigger` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): When the engine starts a micro-batch. processingTime: one every ISO-8601 duration. availableNow: true: read what the topic holds now, in as many batches as it takes, then stop (a scheduled catch-up run). Absent: derived from the expose's qos.freshnessSLO. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.trigger.processingTime` | string | yes | matches `^P(?!$)(\d+Y)?(\d+M)?(\d+W)?(\d+D)?(T(\d+H)?(\d+M)?(\d+S)?)?$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. ISO-8601 duration (e.g., P1D, PT15M, P2Y6M). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.trigger.availableNow` | boolean | yes | must be `true` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.watermark` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The event-time watermark: the timestamp column it follows and how late a record may arrive before stateful operators drop it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.watermark.column` | string | yes | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. A timestamp column of the stream, or a nested field of one as a dotted path. On a Spark build it must be timestamp_ltz: Spark refuses a watermark on TIMESTAMP_NTZ (EVENT_TIME_IS_NOT_ON_TIMESTAMP_TYPE), and the Spark compiler refuses a timestamp (no time zone) watermark column. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.watermark.delay` | string | yes | matches `^P(?!$)(\d+Y)?(\d+M)?(\d+W)?(\d+D)?(T(\d+H)?(\d+M)?(\d+S)?)?$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The allowed lateness, as an ISO-8601 duration (PT10M). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.checkpoint` | string | no | matches `^s3://[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9](?:/[^\u0000-\u001f\u007f]*)?(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Where the engine keeps its offsets and state, as an s3:// URI. Absent: derived from the product's Iceberg warehouse, one location per product and build. The checkpoint is the job's position in the topic: moving it starts the job again from startingOffsets. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.startingOffsets` | string | no | one of `earliest`, `latest` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Where a job with no checkpoint yet starts reading: earliest (all the topic retains) or latest (new records only). Absent: the engine's default, latest for a Spark stream. A job that has a checkpoint resumes from it. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.maxOffsetsPerTrigger` | integer | no | min 1<br>max 9223372036854775807 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The most Kafka records one micro-batch reads, split across the topic's partitions by their backlog (Spark's maxOffsetsPerTrigger). It bounds a batch's size and memory when a stream catches up: after a stop, or from earliest. Absent: no limit, so one batch reads everything waiting. A Spark stream only: managed Flink refuses the key. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter` | object | no | When `sink` is `topic`: must not set `table`<br>When `sink` is `topic`: requires `topic`<br>When `sink` is `topic`: a topic sink names its topic, and no table<br>When not (`sink` is `topic`): must not set `topic`<br>When not (`sink` is `topic`): topic is for sink: topic; a table sink takes table |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): What forge's Spark runner does with a record it cannot land: a value or key that is not the declared JSON, a field of another type, or a required field that is null (an Avro stream's dead letters are not supported yet). With deadLetter, each such record goes to a dead-letter sink, with its raw bytes, the reason, and its topic, partition and offset, and the stream keeps running; without it, or with enabled: false, the first such record fails the stream. The keys follow the acquisition lane's dlq (enabled, maxRecordsBeforeAbort, alertOn). A Spark stream only: managed Flink refuses the key. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.enabled` | boolean | no |  | `true` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. false: no dead letters; a record that cannot land fails the stream (an overlay can switch it off per environment). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.sink` | string | no | one of `table`, `topic` | `"table"` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. table: an Iceberg table beside the output, in the output's catalog and database. topic: a Kafka topic on the cluster the stream reads, each record keyed by where it came from (&lt;topic&gt;-&lt;partition&gt;@&lt;offset&gt;), its own key in the fluid.dead-letter.raw-key header, and Kafka Connect's error-context headers (__connect.errors.topic, .partition, .offset, .exception.message). Sent at least once: a batch sent again after a failure carries the same keys, so a consumer can drop repeats by key. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.table` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,254}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. sink table only: the table's name in the output's database. Absent: &lt;output table&gt;__dead_letter, as late events go to &lt;output table&gt;__late_events. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.topic` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,249}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. sink topic only, and required there: the dead-letter topic, on the cluster the stream reads. It must exist; the job writes to it and creates nothing. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.maxRecordsBeforeAbort` | integer | no | min 0 | `10000` | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The stream fails once it has sent more dead letters than this since it started (0: the first one fails it, after it has landed in the sink). |
| `builds[].properties.stream.deadLetter.alertOn` | array of string | no | unique items<br>each item: one of `schema_violation` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The reasons the runner logs a dead_letter_alert line for, each micro-batch that sends any: schema_violation is every record the stream could not land. |

The output column, or a field of a struct output column as a dotted path (customer.id). Mapping a nested field builds that struct from the paths given, so a nested output can be written from fields that are flat or elsewhere in the record. |
| `builds[].properties.mapping.columns[].from` | string | yes | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\|\['[^'\\\u0000-\u001f\u007f]{1,256}'\])*(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The raw value never reaches the table, and a keyed digest cannot be reversed by hashing a dictionary of likely values. Opt-in: the default masking is a protected view derived from the table. |

The package as its team published it, a .whl or a .zip: s3://&lt;bucket&gt;/&lt;key&gt; for the AWS runtimes, file:///&lt;path&gt; on the machine fluid apply runs on for runtime local. On AWS fluid apply copies the object into the build's artifact prefix only when S3's SHA-256 checksum of it is the pin, so publish it single-part with --checksum-algorithm SHA256 (aws s3api put-object). The operator lists where packages may come from in FLUID_SPARK_PACKAGE_ALLOWLIST. |

NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): What forge's Spark runner does with a row of a package's output that fails the contract's checks: a required value that is null, at any depth. With deadLetter, each such row goes to an Iceberg table beside the output, with the reason, the row as JSON, the run and the package's sha256, and the run writes the other rows; without it, or with enabled: false, any such row fails the run and nothing is written. The keys follow properties.stream.deadLetter. |

### alerts

| Path | Type | Required | Allowed values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alerts` | object | no |  |  | NEW in v0.7.7: Who hears about the failures, retries, successes and missed SLAs of the DAGs forge generates for this product, and how. Each route names a kind and the scheduler connection that holds the address, URL or key; the secret is never in the contract. |
| `alerts.sla` | string | no | matches `^P(?=\d\|T\d)(\d{1,7}W)?(\d{1,7}D)?(T(?=\d)(\d{1,7}H)?(\d{1,7}M)?(\d{1,7}S)?)?$` |  | How long a run may take before its sla_miss routes alert, as an ISO-8601 duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds (PT4H, P1DT6H), at most P30D. On Airflow 2 it is every task's sla, measured from the end of the run's data interval (its scheduled start); on Airflow 3.1+, which has no SLAs, a deadline alert that long after the run was queued. |
| `alerts.defaults` | boolean | no |  | `true` | Whether the product takes the default routes of the organisation's installed packs (the fluid_build.alert_defaults entry points). |
| `alerts.routes` | array of object | no | max items 20 |  |  |
| `alerts.routes[].name` | string | yes | matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` |  |  |
| `alerts.routes[].kind` | string | yes | matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` |  | email (SmtpNotifier), slack (SlackWebhookNotifier), webhook (HttpNotifier, see format), pagerduty (PagerdutyNotifier), or a kind an installed package registers under the fluid_build.alert_notifiers entry points. |
| `alerts.routes[].events` | array of string | no | min items 1<br>unique items<br>each item: one of `failure`, `retry`, `success`, `sla_miss` | `["failure"]` | What the route alerts on. success resolves an incident a failure opened (zenduty and opsgenie formats, pagerduty). sla_miss needs alerts.sla. |
| `alerts.routes[].connection` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,249}$` |  | The Airflow connection id that holds the address, URL or key: the scheduler's secrets backend serves it. Required for webhook; email, slack and pagerduty default to smtp_default, slack_default and pagerduty_events_default. |
| `alerts.routes[].to` | array of string | no | min items 1<br>max items 50<br>each item: matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}@[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,63}(\.[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,63})+$` |  | email only: the addresses to send to. |
| `alerts.routes[].from` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}@[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,63}(\.[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,63})+$` |  | email only: the sender; without it the SMTP connection's from_email (or Airflow 2's \[smtp\] smtp_mail_from). |
| `alerts.routes[].format` | string | no | one of `generic`, `zenduty`, `opsgenie` |  | webhook only: the JSON the route posts. generic is forge's own document; zenduty a Zenduty Generic Integration event (the integration URL is the connection's host); opsgenie an Opsgenie Alert API request (the alerts URL is the host, the GenieKey header is in the connection's extra). |
| `alerts.routes[].severity` | string | no | one of `critical`, `error`, `warning`, `info` |  | The severity of the route's failure, retry and sla_miss alerts; by default critical for failure and warning for retry and sla_miss. |
| `alerts.routes[].options` | object (free-form) | no |  |  | A plugin kind's own settings: JSON values whose strings hold no '{' or '}', no URL and no secret. |

| `packaging.containers.kmsKey` | string | no | one of `isolated`, `shared` |  | NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): Ownership of the KMS key (aws_kms_key) that encrypts the product's data, checkpoints and logs. |

| `exposes[].contract.schema[].type` | description | Column data type. Accepts a canonical FLUID/SQL type name (case-insensitive) or a parameterized form such as decimal(18,4) or varchar(255). The enum lists the canonical bare types; the pattern additionally permits case variants and parameter suffixes. Intentionally generous — it rejects obvious garbage (e.g. MYSTERY_TYPE) while admitting the cross-dialect superset. | Column data type. Accepts a canonical FLUID/SQL type name (case-insensitive) or a parameterized form such as decimal(18,4) or varchar(255). The enum lists the canonical bare types; the pattern additionally permits case variants and parameter suffixes. An enum names its levels in its parameter list, comma-separated: each level is a word list (enum(IE, United Kingdom)) or a quoted string that may hold any character but a control character, with its own quote doubled, as in SQL string literals (enum('Dr.', '&gt;10000', 'O''Brien', 'a, b')). Intentionally generous — it rejects obvious garbage (e.g. MYSTERY_TYPE) while admitting the cross-dialect superset. |

Kind↔platform mapping: bucket → aws_s3_bucket / google_storage_bucket; database → snowflake_database AND aws_glue_catalog_database; dataset → google_bigquery_dataset; schema → snowflake_schema; warehouse → snowflake_warehouse; cluster → Confluent environment/cluster (v1: shared only). | `builds[].engine` | description | Build/ingestion engine. Transformation engines: dbt, sql, python, spark, glue, custom. Adapter-qualified dbt engines (dbt-&lt;adapter&gt;, e.g. dbt-glue, dbt-snowflake, dbt-bigquery) are accepted too and route through the dbt build runner, which derives the adapter from the suffix. Ingestion engines (acquisition pattern only): duckdb (zero-infra files/JDBC), airbyte (350+ SaaS), meltano (Singer 600+ taps), dlt (Python-native), kafka-connect (streaming), debezium (CDC). AWS Glue: glue (Spark ETL jobs managed by Glue). NEW in v0.7.6: flink (Apache Flink jobs, usually long-running streaming SQL with properties.language: flink_sql). forge-cli validates and plans a flink build but ships no runner for it: the platform that runs the job, such as the Flink Kubernetes Operator or AWS Managed Service for Apache Flink, executes it. Put deployment settings under properties.parameters, for example parallelism and upgradeMode, as the Flink Kubernetes Operator's job spec names them, and flinkConfiguration. | Build/ingestion engine. Transformation engines: dbt, sql, python, spark, glue, custom. Adapter-qualified dbt engines (dbt-&lt;adapter&gt;, e.g. dbt-glue, dbt-snowflake, dbt-bigquery) are accepted too and route through the dbt build runner, which derives the adapter from the suffix. Ingestion engines (acquisition pattern only): duckdb (zero-infra files/JDBC), airbyte (350+ SaaS), meltano (Singer 600+ taps), dlt (Python-native), kafka-connect (streaming), debezium (CDC). AWS Glue: glue (Spark ETL jobs managed by Glue). NEW in v0.7.6: flink (Apache Flink jobs, usually long-running streaming SQL with properties.language: flink_sql). forge-cli validates and plans a flink build but ships no runner for it: the platform that runs the job, such as the Flink Kubernetes Operator or AWS Managed Service for Apache Flink, executes it. Put deployment settings under properties.parameters, for example parallelism and upgradeMode, as the Flink Kubernetes Operator's job spec names them, and flinkConfiguration. NEW in v0.7.7: lakeflow (a Databricks Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline: pattern embedded-logic, properties.sql is the SELECT of the dataset an expose binds; forge-cli writes the materialized view around it, with the expose's columns and its dq.rules as pipeline expectations, and fluid apply provisions one serverless pipeline per build). |

The ASCII part of Airflow's rule: letters (either case), digits, underscore, dot and dash, at most 250 characters. Airflow's own pattern, ^\[\\w.-\]+$, also takes the Unicode letters and digits that \\w matches, which an id here may not hold. |

Schemes: env, file, vault, aws-sm, gcp-sm, azure-kv; aliases openbao (vault), aws (aws-sm), gcp (gcp-sm) and azure (azure-kv) are accepted; any other lower-case scheme (such as op://) is passed to the pack that resolves it. #field picks one key of a secret that holds several; ?version= pins a version where the store keeps them. |
| `packaging.containers` | description | NEW in v0.7.6: Per-container-kind ownership overrides — each key wins over `mode` for that kind, yielding hybrid tiers. Kind↔platform mapping: bucket → aws_s3_bucket / google_storage_bucket; database → snowflake_database AND aws_glue_catalog_database; dataset → google_bigquery_dataset; schema → snowflake_schema; warehouse → snowflake_warehouse; cluster → Confluent environment/cluster (v1: shared only). | NEW in v0.7.6: Per-container-kind ownership overrides — each key wins over `mode` for that kind, yielding hybrid tiers. Kind↔platform mapping: bucket → aws_s3_bucket / google_storage_bucket; database → snowflake_database AND aws_glue_catalog_database; dataset → google_bigquery_dataset; schema → snowflake_schema; warehouse → snowflake_warehouse; cluster → Confluent environment/cluster (v1: shared only). NEW in v0.7.7 (preview), AWS streaming kinds: lfTagVocabulary → aws_lakeformation_lf_tag (the domain's LF-tag keys and values); emrApplication → aws_emrserverless_application; schemaRegistry → aws_glue_registry; athenaWorkgroup → aws_athena_workgroup; kmsKey → aws_kms_key (the domain key); mwaaEnvironment → aws_mwaa_environment (shared only: the platform team owns it, and a product ships DAG files into it). These kinds are not part of the blanket mode's plan summary; a product reads each one's decision explicitly. |

None. Every 0.7.6 field path is present in 0.7.7.
